activities.title: Fill the Total Cost column in one move
activities.intro: Open your Lab 3 inventory in your own spreadsheet app. Write one formula, fill it down, then answer from your own file.

items: Click E2 and type =C2*D2, then press Enter.
Click E2 again. Double-click the fill handle at its bottom-right corner.
Press Ctrl + ` (the key under Esc) to show formulas. Check what E9 says. Press it again to go back.

blocks.prompt: In Formulas view, what formula does E9 show?

help: No data yet? Type 3 rows: A4 paper 25 × 245, long paper 30 × 265, ballpen 10 × 96.
Use the asterisk * to multiply, not the letter x.
Stop at row 9. Do not fill into the TOTAL row.
Seeing #VALUE!? A number was typed with a ₱ sign or a space. Type the plain number again.
In LibreOffice, show formulas with View, Show Formula.

activities.title: Add a 12% VAT column: break it, then fix it
activities.intro: First you will see the column of zeros on purpose, then fix it with one $ lock. Work in your own inventory file.

items: In A12 type VAT rate; in B12 type 12%. In G1 type VAT 12%.
In G2 type =E2*B12 and fill down to G9. See the zeros?
Fix G2: click after B12, press F4 to get $B$12, press Enter, then fill down again.
Stretch: in H1 type Total with VAT, in H2 type =E2+G2, and fill down.

blocks.prompt: After the fix, what is the result in G10?
After the fix, what is the value in G3?
What formula is in G2 after the fix?
Stretch: which reference style did H2 =E2+G2 need?

help: G10 shows 735.00? Your G column still points to B13 and below. Lock the rate as $B$12 and fill down again.
F4 does nothing? Try Fn + F4 on a laptop, Cmd + T in Excel for Mac, or Shift + F4 in LibreOffice Calc.
You can also type the $ signs by hand. The result is the same.

blocks.prompt: G2 holds =E2*B12. You fill it down to G5. What does G5 contain?
